title: What fraction of a circle is a cone's curved surface?
description: A cone has base radius five centimetres and slant length ten centimetres. The board matches the curved edge of the flat piece with the distance round the base, then compares it with the full circle of radius ten centimetres. Keeko's doubt is that it is a quarter of the circle.
teaching_notes: One idea: the curved edge of the unrolled cone equals the distance round its base, so the fraction of the circle is the curved edge divided by the full circle's edge. Watch for students who guess the fraction by halving the radius twice.

video_script.why: The child finds what part of a circle a cone's curved surface is by matching its curved edge with the distance round the base, because the flat piece wraps once round the base.
video_script.substitution: base radius 5 cm, slant length 10 cm; curved edge 2 x pi x 5 = 10 pi; full circle of radius 10 cm has circumference 2 x pi x 10 = 20 pi; fraction 10 pi / 20 pi = 1/2.
video_script.anchor: the cone of the book opened out flat into a piece of a circle of radius 10 cm
video_script.wrong_answer: it is a quarter of the circle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko halves the radius, five is half of ten, then halves again to get a quarter; the fraction comes from comparing the curved edge with the full circle, which gives a half, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The curved surface is half of the circle, a semicircle of radius ten centimetres

final_answer.value: Half of the circle: a semicircle of radius 10 cm
final_answer.spoken: half of the circle, a semicircle of radius ten centimetres

hold_back: Half of the circle: a semicircle of radius 10 cm
maths_rules: the flat piece is part of a circle whose radius is the slant length, 10 cm
its curved edge wraps once round the base: 2 x pi x 5 = 10 pi
the full circle of radius 10 cm has circumference 2 x pi x 10 = 20 pi
the same result as base radius divided by slant length: 5 / 10 = 1/2
wrong idea: halving 5 to 10 and then halving again gives 1/4, which does not match the lengths
video_script.design: One idea: the curved edge of the flat piece wraps round the base. The cone opens flat on the stage; the base circle and the curved edge are traced in the same colour.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a cone.
<bookmark mark='cone'/>Its base has radius five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='slant'/>The slant length means the distance from the tip of the cone down its side to the rim. Here it is ten centimetres.
<bookmark mark='flat'/>Open the curved surface out flat. It is a piece of a circle of radius ten centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What fraction of the full circle is this piece?

narration: <bookmark mark='edge'/>Step one, the curved edge of the flat piece goes once round the base.
<bookmark mark='circ'/>The distance once round a circle is called its circumference. For the base it is two times pi times five. That is ten pi.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: full circle of radius 10 cm: circumference = 2 x pi x 10 = 20 pi cm

<bookmark mark='twenty'/>It is two times pi times ten, which is twenty pi.

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Step three, divide the curved edge by the circumference of the full circle.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Ten pi divided by twenty pi is one half.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks it is a quarter of the circle. Five is half of ten, and half again is a quarter.
